title: Design System: PalisadeCode v2 — Dragon Fire Workbench

parents: .impeccable/design.json (Palisade Code — Dragon Fire Console: color palette, two-voice type, Spec/Go mode, chat/diff/spec components)
.impeccable/axiom-design.json (Axiom Code Workbench: narrow rail, file explorer, editor-dominant layout, ambient backdrop, tight chrome, breadcrumbs, status bar)
source.mergeStrategy: Palisade palette + Axiom flow. Keep Dragon Fire Green as the sole accent but apply Axiom's scarcity discipline. Adopt Axiom's narrow navigation rail, repository explorer column, editor-dominant center, warm ambient backdrop, floating window shell, traffic lights, breadcrumbs, and status bar. Tighten radii from Palisade's 8/16px to Axiom's 6/8/12px. Reframe Palisade's chat/diff/spec components as panels inside the editor-dominant layout rather than equal-weight columns.

display.purpose: Headings and the brand wordmark. Tight leading (0.96), display tracking (-0.0275em). Same family as body; hierarchy comes from size and weight.

body.purpose: All human-readable prose, UI labels, button text, chat content, input. 1.5 leading, normal tracking, antialiased.

mono.purpose: File paths, timestamps, line numbers, kbd hints, uppercase micro-labels, note editor body, diff content, breadcrumbs, status bar, editor tabs. The machine voice — never used for prose.

chrome.purpose: Tight navigation rail labels, mode-switch segments, status-bar metadata, and window controls. Same family as body but set at 11px with 0.04em tracking for compact density. Adopted from Axiom to resolve the AI-sloppy read — Palisade's 14px UI labels felt web-app-y; 11px chrome reads as a native tool.

shadows.name: flat
shadows.purpose: Default for all resting panels, sidebars, chat bubbles, thread items, tabs. The console is flat-first.

shadows.name: ring
shadows.purpose: The crisp 1px dividing edge, expressed as a ring so it reads as a border rather than a shadow.

shadows.name: window
shadows.purpose: The floating application window. A soft black drop shadow plus a 1px green-tinted ring that ties the window edge to the Dragon Fire accent. Adopted from Axiom, tinted green.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Floating layers only: active mode button, command-bar box, toast, handoff console.

shadows.name: handoff-ambient
shadows.purpose: Green-tinted ambient glow on the handoff console during the mode-transition ritual.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: 2px Dragon Fire Green halo at 45% opacity around focused interactive elements. Tightened from Palisade's 3px/40% to match Axiom's leaner focus.

motion.name: micro
motion.purpose: Hover and active-state changes on navigation, tabs, and file-tree rows. Adopted from Axiom for snappier chrome.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Quick state transitions: tab cross-fade, checklist toggle, pane opacity swap.

motion.name: base
motion.purpose: Default transition for sidebar collapse/expand, banner show/hide, toast slide.

motion.name: handoff-spin
motion.purpose: The handoff glow ring rotation. The sole long animation, reserved for the mode-transition ritual.

motion.name: diff-flash
motion.purpose: Freshly-applied addition lines flash from 40% green to the 6% green resting background.

breakpoints.name: cocktail-rail
breakpoints.purpose: Below 920px the sidebars detach from flex flow and become position:fixed overlays anchored under the top chrome at z-index 50. Above 920px they live in the flex row and collapse by negative margin.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Below 760px the file explorer column hides entirely and the navigation rail collapses to icon-only. The editor takes the full center.

components.name: Window Shell
components.description: Floating desktop window with warm dark chrome, clipped 12px outer corners, and a soft black shadow with a 1px green-tinted ring. Adopted from Axiom to give the app a native-tool presence instead of a web-app full-bleed. The window sits over the Twilight Ember backdrop.

narrative.northStar: The Dragon Fire Workbench: a dark, compact coding cockpit where the editor owns the brightest colors and one restrained green accent signals what is alive. The agent console lives inside the editor, not the other way around.
narrative.overview:
PalisadeCode v2 is a desktop coding-agent workbench, not a chat app. The whole interface lives inside a floating window with 12px clipped corners, sitting over a warm Twilight Ember backdrop. The layout is a four-column cockpit: a narrow 193px navigation rail (threads and workspace), a 143px repository explorer (file tree), the editor-dominant center (tabs, breadcrumbs, code/diff surface, status bar), and a 300px right sidebar (Code Map / Files / Notes, collapsed by default). The agent chat is a panel within the editor column, not an equal-weight column — this is the key shift from v1.

The product's core gesture remains the Spec / Go mode toggle, now a compact pill switch in the 36px top chrome. Spec Mode is read-only planning: the agent replies with spec checklists, the editor is locked, the status bar reads 'Spec Mode' in muted. Go Mode is instant-apply: the editor flips to the diff tab, the status bar reads 'Go Mode' in Dragon Fire Green, applied additions flash green. The visual system signals mode through the status bar, the tab emphasis, and the chat content shape — no more full-width banner.

The color palette is unchanged from v1: a near-black field, two charcoal surfaces, one Dragon Fire Green accent, and three semantic status hues. What changes is discipline: the accent is scarcer (Axiom's lesson), the chrome is tighter (11px type, 6px radii), the editor owns the syntax colors, and the warm ambient backdrop replaces the flat black field. The result reads as a native code tool, not an AI chat app.
keyCharacteristics: Editor-dominant layout. The code/diff surface is the largest and brightest area; navigation and chat are supporting panels, not equal-weight columns. This is the primary fix for the AI-sloppy read.
Narrow navigation rail (193px) + file explorer (143px). Adopted from Axiom. The app reads as a code tool because the file tree is visible, not hidden behind a chat feed.
Warm ambient backdrop. The Twilight Ember backdrop (deep warm green-black) sits behind the floating window, giving depth without cocoa warmth. Replaces v1's flat black full-bleed.
Tight chrome. 36px top chrome, 28px tab strip, 18px status bar, 11px UI type with 0.04em tracking. Adopted from Axiom. v1's 56px nav and 14px labels read as web-app; v2 reads as native tool.

Scarce glowing accent. Dragon Fire Green appears only on: the active thread rail, the send button, the branch badge, the breadcrumb active segment, the Go Mode status indicator, diff additions, the focus ring, and the spec badge. Never on chrome, dividers, or decoration.
Two-voice typography. Sans for prose and UI labels; mono for files, paths, code, breadcrumbs, status bar, tabs, and metadata. Unchanged from v1 — the two-voice split is load-bearing.

Quiet motion, 120–200ms. Micro (120ms) for chrome hover/active; fast (150ms) for tab cross-fade and pane swap; base (200ms) for sidebar collapse and toast slide. The handoff spinner (1s linear) is the only long animation.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Dragon Fire Green is the only chromatic brand color; it is reserved for live, actionable, or agent-active surfaces: active thread rail, send button, branch badge, breadcrumb active segment, Go Mode status, diff additions, focus ring, spec badge. Never use it for decoration, dividers, or static chrome. Adopted from v1, enforced harder — Axiom's gold discipline applied to green.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: If the user reads it as a sentence, it's the sans; if the user reads it as a path, a timestamp, a key, or a label, it's the mono. Never set prose in monospace, never set a file path in the sans. Unchanged from v1.

rules.name: The Editor-Dominant Rule
rules.body: The editor (code or diff surface) is the largest and brightest area of the workbench. Navigation, file tree, and chat are supporting panels with lower contrast. The editor owns the syntax colors; chrome stays muted. This is the primary fix for the AI-sloppy read — v1 gave chat equal weight to code.

rules.name: The Narrow-Rail Rule
rules.body: Left navigation rail is 193px; file explorer is 143px. Both are narrow enough that the editor dominates the viewport. They collapse by sliding out via negative margin over 200ms — they do not overlay. Below 760px the file explorer hides and the rail goes icon-only. Adopted from Axiom.

rules.name: The Flat-First Rule
rules.body: Borders divide; shadows elevate only what floats above the field (the window shell, command bar, toast, handoff console, active mode pill). Never shadow a resting panel. Unchanged from v1, now including the window shell as a floating layer.

rules.name: The Three-Radius Rule
rules.body: Use 6px for controls, buttons, list items, tabs, and inline elements; use 8px for cards, chat bubbles, the command-bar box, and the diff panel; use 12px only for the outer window shell; use 9999px (pill) exclusively for the mode switch, branch badge, spec badge, and status indicators. Tightened from v1's 8/16px — Axiom's 6px controls read as a native tool, not a web app.

dos: Do let the editor own the brightest colors — syntax highlighting is the visual center, not the chat.
Do keep the navigation rail at 193px and the file explorer at 143px so the editor dominates.
Do use 11px chrome type with 0.04em tracking for navigation, tabs, status bar, and window controls.
Do reserve Dragon Fire Green for live/actionable surfaces only — active thread rail, send button, branch badge, breadcrumb active, Go Mode status, diff additions, focus ring.
Do set file paths, breadcrumbs, status bar, tabs, and code in the monospace voice; set prose and UI labels in the sans voice.
Do use 6px radius for controls, 8px for cards, 12px for the window shell, and pill for status capsules only.
Do show the file tree by default — it is what makes the app read as a code tool.
Do invert the toast (fg-on-bg) so it reads as a system utterance distinct from the dark chrome.
donts: Don't give the chat panel equal weight to the editor — chat is a supporting panel, not a co-star.
Don't introduce a second brand chromatic color. Twilight Glow is the only green-adjacent tone; everything else is neutral or semantic status.
Don't use 14px or 16px UI type in chrome — 11px is the chrome size. Larger sizes are for chat content and editor prose only.
Don't use 16px radius for anything — the largest radius is 12px (window shell only). Cards and chat bubbles use 8px; controls use 6px.
Don't shadow resting panels. Shadows are for the window shell, command bar, toast, handoff console, and active mode pill only.
Don't set prose in monospace or file paths in the sans — the two-voice split is load-bearing.
Don't use the accent for borders, dividers, or static chrome; the border color is the only divider.
Don't hide the file tree behind a tab or toggle — it is a permanent column at desktop width.
